questions.q: According to the summary, what should be your aim when starting a business?
a: Building something you believe in enough to fight for
Selling the company within two or three years
Raising as much investor money as possible
Copying the largest competitor's business model
questions.why: Lesson 1 warns that if selling is your only goal you will never get there, and urges you to build something worth standing for.

questions.q: What does the summary say about corporate jargon in marketing?
a: It sounds pretentious and nobody really understands it
It makes a small company look trustworthy
It is required when selling to other businesses
It saves time compared with plain writing
questions.why: Lesson 2 says buzzword-heavy copy makes companies sound pretentious rather than clear or honest.

questions.q: How does the summary suggest you should write to customers?
a: The way you would talk to a friend
In the formal tone of a press release
With as many technical terms as possible
Using slogans borrowed from big brands
questions.why: Lesson 2 recommends plain, honest writing instead of imitating the language of large corporations.

questions.q: What happens when someone stays late at the office, per the summary?
a: Everyone else feels bad for not staying late too
The whole team becomes more productive
Your manager rewards you with more freedom
You finish work you could not do earlier
questions.why: Lesson 3 says late nights mostly make colleagues feel guilty and do not produce the extra output people imagine.

questions.q: Why are long meetings costly, according to the summary?
a: Ten people in a one-hour meeting lose ten hours of focus
They require expensive equipment to run well
They always produce decisions nobody follows
They force everyone to work overtime afterward
questions.why: Lesson 3 multiplies a 10-person, one-hour meeting into 10 hours of lost focused work.
